Of the 1,872 specimens, 55 (2.9% [CI = 2.2%–3.7%]) were positive for CrAg.
The prevalence of cryptococcal antigenemia was 2.9% (95% confidence interval = 2.2%–3.7%).
Persons with a CD4 count >50 cells/ µ L were less likely to be CrAg-positive
Serum specimens randomly selected from those eligible were tested using the CrAg LFA.
